time.desc: Audit Institution A resigned from the audit work and questioned the company's integrity and moral commitment. The company's stock price fell by nearly 50% in two days, and its market value fell below the index A threshold.
The company submitted a compliance plan to the exchange and hired Audit Institution B as a new auditor. The stock price rose by more than 30% in a single day.
The exchange approved the company's extension to submit its financial report application, allowing it to maintain listing and trading status before October 1
The company was officially excluded from the exchange product H, and the stock price fell 8% that day.
The company submitted overdue annual and quarterly reports to regulatory agencies and successfully avoided delisting. The stock price soared by more than 24% after the market closed.
The company disclosed that there were major flaws in the internal control of financial reporting and failed to operate effectively, and the stock price fell 5.5% that day.
The company’s CEO was arrested on suspicion of illegally smuggling high-end chips to Country X and faces multiple federal criminal charges
The company's director resigned, and the board of directors launched an independent investigation to verify employees' suspected chip smuggling.

The company did not clarify the time for submitting the annual report, causing the stock price to plummet by about 20% in a single day. The investment bank downgraded the rating to underweight and significantly reduced the target price.

The company announced that it would not be able to submit its quarterly report on time and lowered its quarterly revenue forecast, warning that delisting might trigger the early repayment of huge amounts of convertible bonds.

The company's stock price surged by more than 30% in a single day, but it is still down by about 75% from the historical high during the year, and the price-to-earnings ratio dropped to a single-digit discount.

The exchange approved the extension of the listing period to a specified date and required the company to submit overdue annual and quarterly reports before that. The CEO expressed confidence that the standards would be met.

The special committee announced the final investigation results, saying that no fraud was found by management or the board of directors, and there was no need to restate historical financial reports. The stock price soared by about 30% in a single day.

The company was approved by the exchange to extend the compliance period, and the stock price rose sharply before the market opened. An independent investigation showed that the management had no wrongdoing and that the resignation of the previous auditor lacked factual basis.

The exchange formally approved the company's application to postpone the submission of annual financial documents, the stock continued to be listed under the supervision of a new external auditor, and analysts raised the target price
The exchange announced that the company would be removed from the large company index and replaced by other companies. Affected by this, the company's stock price fell by about 8% that day.

The founder of the short-selling agency that once attacked the company and raised questions about its financial fraud announced the dissolution of the agency, saying that the phased tasks had been completed and the latest investigation information had been shared with regulatory agencies.

The original audit agency submitted a resignation letter, stating that the company's financial reports were too suspicious and that it no longer relied on the statements of management and the audit committee.
The company disclosed the third revision of the loan agreement, extending the period for providing audited financial documents and adding a minimum unlimited cash clause
The resignation of the auditor raised concerns about index deletion, and the company issued a business update after the close saying it was actively looking for a new auditor.
The company received a non-compliance notification letter from the exchange, confirming that it violated the listing rules due to delay in submitting annual and quarterly reports.
Analysts rated the hiring of a new auditor as a major positive development, and the company's stock price rebounded nearly 80% in a single week.
The Board of Directors adopted the recommendations of the Special Committee, appointed a new Chief Accounting Officer and approved transition arrangements for the Chief Financial Officer.
The company's stock price rose by about 30% in a single day as the investigation results were revealed.
Analysts raised the company's target price, anticipating a return of investors after the regulatory decision was announced.
